sources.entry: Credyt - Real-time monetization infrastructure for AI-native products. Credyt combines cost and profitability observabilty with usage-based monetization and a managed customer billing UX.

summary.name: Credyt
summary.one_liner: Credyt is real-time monetization infrastructure for AI products, combining per-customer AI cost observability, budget enforcement, and usage-based billing with a customer billing portal.
keywords: how to charge for ai product
use_cases: Billing AI product users per token or per request
Tracking which customers are unprofitable due to AI compute costs
Setting hard spend limits per customer or agent
Adding a customer-facing billing portal without frontend work
Testing new pricing models without a code deployment
summary.what_it_does: Credyt streams cost data for each API call, model, and customer, so teams can see per-customer costs and profitability as usage happens. It checks a customer's balance before authorising usage and blocks actions when the balance is insufficient, which is intended to prevent spend beyond set limits. Pricing can be designed in a dashboard and changed without code, and it supports usage-based, subscription, hybrid, credits, token, and entitlement models. Customers get a billing portal showing live balance, usage history, and top-up options. The page says usage is authorised, priced, and debited atomically, with webhooks fired on balance updates.
notable: Real-time balance check and debit before AI usage is authorised, not after invoicing
Supports many pricing models (usage, subscription, hybrid, credits, tokens, entitlements) configured in a dashboard
Team founded by people from Visa, Checkout.com, TrueLayer, and SumUp, per the page
caveats: Pricing is described as free to start, charged per active customer rather than as a revenue percentage; specific paid tier amounts are not stated on the page
Listing describes it as a tool for AI-native products; page does not name specific supported AI providers beyond example model names
